title: What to say in a case interview: useful phrases for every stage
description: The phrases strong candidates use at each of the ten stages of a case interview, from the first recap to the final recommendation.
hook: Sometimes the hardest part of a case is simply knowing what words to say next. Here are the phrases strong candidates use at each stage, so you always have a sentence ready. Use them as a starting point, then make them sound like you.
body:
1. Listen and take notes

Listen and note

"Thank you for the case, this is an interesting problem."

Don’t fake understanding

"Before I recap, one quick check: when you said X, did you mean...?"

Draw early insights

"Interesting that revenue fell while volume held. I may want to come back to pricing."

2. Recap

Recap the key points only

"So our client is X, facing Y, and success means Z by [date]. Did I get that right?"

3. Clarifying questions (three at most)

Pick the questions that matter

"How does the client actually make money?" / "Is there a specific target and timeline for this goal?"

Ask to build, not to stall

"Is this a problem the whole industry is facing, or just our client?"

Ask for thinking time

"Thank you, that’s useful. May I take a moment to structure my thoughts?"

4. Structure

Present it top-down

"There are three areas I want to look at. First... I believe the second, the unit economics, is most likely the issue, so I’d start there."

5. Lead the case

Propose, don’t wait

"As a next step, I’d like market data to test whether the decline is industry-wide. Do we have anything on that?"

Summarise at the turns

"Let me quickly summarise where we are: we know A and B; the open question is C."

6. Charts and exhibits

Take a moment

"Thank you. May I take a moment to process this?"

Insights, not description

"Two things stand out. First... Second... Given our goal, the second matters more, and I’d like to quantify it."

If stuck or wrong

"I’d like to take a step back. We know A, B and C, and we’re trying to get to X."

7. Maths

Approach before arithmetic

"My approach: market size × our share × margin gives yearly profit, and I’d compare that with the investment to get the payback. Does that make sense before I run the numbers?"

Always sanity-check

"Quick sanity check: 2M units at $50 is $100M, consistent with a $500M market at 20% share. Good."

Market sizing extras

"Before I size it, my rough guess is a few hundred million dollars a year. Let me test that top-down."

8. Brainstorm

Structure even here

"Let me think about this in two buckets: what we can do with today’s capabilities, and what needs new ones. On the first..."

Add one real example

"Retention offers work well here; it’s what mobile operators do when contracts end."

9. Recommendation

Answer first

"I recommend entering through a joint venture. Two reasons: the market grows 12% a year, and a partner caps our investment at $20M with breakeven in year 2. The key risk is depending on the partner, so as next steps I’d agree exit terms and test demand in one city."

Park what you didn’t cover

"...and as a next step I’d also look at the cost side, which we didn’t get to today."

10. Throughout the case

Link everything back

"...and this matters because our client’s goal is X."

Make them yours

These are starting points, not a script. Say them in your own words, at your own pace. Interviewers respond to someone who sounds natural and clear, not someone who sounds rehearsed.
outro: You do not have to get all of this right at once. Pick one thing from this guide to focus on in your next practice case.
